security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences and inline code formatting, not executable Ruby backtick syntax. I found one contextual risk: the skill documents a destructive Git reset command without explicit confirmation or backup guidance. No prompt injection or data exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before git reset --hard, and recommend git status plus backup or stash steps first.

remediation.issue: Remote Git operations can change shared repositories.
remediation.suggestion: State that push, pull, rebase, and pull request operations should follow project policy and user confirmation.

content.user_title: Manage Git Workflows With Clear Checklists
content.value_statement: Git work can become inconsistent across branches, commits, and pull requests. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structured Git workflows, templates, and review checklists.
actual_capabilities: Provides a feature development checklist from branch creation through merge.
Explains GitHub Flow and Git Flow branch strategies.
Defines conventional commit types and commit message examples.
Supplies a pull request checklist and PR template sections.
Lists common Git commands for daily work, fixes, cherry-pick, bisect, and stash.
limitations: Does not execute Git commands by itself; tool behavior depends on the host assistant.
Does not inspect repository state unless the assistant reads or runs local commands.
Includes destructive command examples that require human confirmation before use.
Does not replace project-specific branching or release policies.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Feature Branch
use_cases.description: Create a branch plan, commit sequence, and merge path before starting feature work.

use_cases.title: Standardize Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Use consistent PR checklists and templates for review-ready changes.

use_cases.title: Teach Git Practices
use_cases.description: Give new contributors clear examples for commits, branches, and safe history cleanup.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Feature Branch
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan a Git workflow for this feature. Include the branch name, commit strategy, update steps, and pull request checklist.

prompt_templates.title: Write Commit Messages
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these planned changes and suggest conventional commit messages. Group related changes and keep each commit atomic.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Pull Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a pull request summary for these changes. Include testing notes, review risks, documentation updates, and merge readiness checks.

prompt_templates.title: Recover From Git Mistakes
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me recover from this Git mistake safely. Ask before any destructive command, explain data-loss risks, and suggest backup steps first.

output_examples.input: I need to start a new authentication feature.
output_examples.output: The skill produces a feature branch plan, an atomic commit outline, update steps from main, and a PR readiness checklist.

output_examples.input: My pull request needs a better description.
output_examples.output: The skill drafts a concise summary, change list, testing notes, documentation status, and review focus areas.

output_examples.input: I made commits in the wrong order.
output_examples.output: The skill explains safe recovery options, highlights destructive commands, and asks for confirmation before history changes.

best_practices: Check repository status before running history-changing commands.
Keep commits atomic and use clear conventional commit messages.
Use the PR checklist before asking reviewers to approve changes.
anti_patterns: Running destructive Git commands without confirming user intent.
Mixing unrelated changes into one commit or pull request.
Rebasing or pushing shared history without team agreement.

faq.question: Does this skill run Git commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow guidance and examples. The host assistant controls any command execution.

faq.question: Can it help with pull request descriptions?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a PR template, checklist, and guidance for summaries, changes, testing, and screenshots.

faq.question: Does it support conventional commits?
faq.answer: Yes. It lists common commit types and provides message examples for features and fixes.

faq.question: Is it suitable for release-based teams?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains both GitHub Flow and Git Flow, including release branch concepts.

faq.question: Can it resolve merge conflicts?
faq.answer: It can guide conflict workflows, but it must inspect repository files or command output to give specific fixes.

faq.question: What safety checks are recommended?
faq.answer: Confirm destructive commands, inspect status first, protect shared history, and avoid committing secrets.
